observations: Photo 0 shows a black metal X-style keyboard stand with four legs, placed on a tiled floor against a textured wall.
Photo 1 shows a keyboard on the stand, with a beige and black front panel, white and black keys, and a small LCD screen. The keyboard appears to be in a room with a textured wall and tiled floor.

Photo 2 shows a top-down view of the same keyboard, revealing the full front panel with buttons, knobs, and a small display. The keyboard is placed on a gray fabric surface, possibly a couch or chair, with a tiled floor visible.
The keyboard has a beige casing with black keys and a black control panel. The brand name is not clearly visible in any photo.
The stand is black metal with a cross-braced design and four legs with rubber feet.
The keyboard appears to be a 61-key model, typical of the CTK 4200 series.
No power adapter or stand is visible in any photo.

claims.claim: Nearly used Casio CTK 4200 Professional Keyboard with Adapter and Stand

No video or photo shows the keyboard powered on or keys being pressed. Functionality cannot be confirmed from still images.
No adapter is visible in any photo. The keyboard is shown on a stand, but no power cable or adapter is present.

claims.claim: Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be a Casio CTK 4200 or may be a different model.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model name on the front panel or back of the keyboard.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic keyboard, not as a specific CTK 4200.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional (keys/buttons not working).
risks.proof: A video clip showing the keyboard powered on, keys being pressed, and sound output.

risks.risk: The stand may be damaged or missing parts (e.g., legs, rubber feet).
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the stand's legs and feet, showing no cracks or missing parts.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a damaged or incomplete stand.

risks.risk: The adapter may be missing or non-functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the adapter and a video showing it connected to the keyboard and powering it on.

proof_requests: Close-up of the sticker with the model number, usually inside the lid or on the bottom.
A clear photo of the model name on the front or back of the keyboard.
A video clip showing the keyboard powered on and keys/buttons working.
A close-up photo of the stand's legs and feet.
A photo of the adapter and a video showing it connected to the keyboard.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
